Similarly, the Zoning Hearing Examiner, the Historic Conservation Board, the Zoning Board of Appeals, or the Building Board of Appeals almost always act in a quasi-judicial capacity. In those circumstances the role of elected officials is limited, as is that of any citizen. Quasi-judicial proceedings are essentially trials. The body hearing the matter is expected to make decisions solely on the record before them and not be influenced by private communications with anyone. Elected officials or their staffs may testify before such bodies, but as with any other witness, they would do so under oath and subject to cross-examination.
